items.title: Anwar: TH investigations can go beyond RCI scope and cover developments up to 2025
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Investigations into issues surrounding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) are not confined to the period covered by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) and can extend beyond 2020, including developments up to 2025. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the RCI served as the main framework for examining issues involving TH, but enforcement and investigative agencies were not restricted from looking into matters that occurred before or after the period covered by the commission. The RCI serves as the main framework.

items.title: Probe launched after premature baby tests positive for prohibited substance
items.summary: Its director, Che Samsuzuki Che Noh, said the department received a referral from the hospital last week after the baby, who required further treatment, underwent the urine screening. He said the hospital also lodged a police report following the test result. Che Samsuzuki said the department conducted further investigations on Aug 12 by visiting the family's home and interviewing the baby's biological mother and father.

items.title: Poor contractor management behind 75 per cent of delayed, sick projects - Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Poor contractor management, weak operational supervision and financial problems account for 75 per cent of delayed and "sick" projects nationwide. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said technical and construction site issues accounted for only 25 per cent of the problems. This, he said, highlights the need for contractors to strengthen their management capabilities and financial position.

items.title: Govt open to studying GST-SST combination for more progressive tax system
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government is open to studying a combination of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Sales and Services Tax (SST) as part of efforts to develop a more progressive tax system. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was prepared to review and improve the country's existing tax system, including considering certain features of GST that could be incorporated into the current SST framework. "We are open to studying ways to improve the tax system.

items.title: Too few facility management contractors despite RM39.59b opportunity
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: The limited number of facility management contractors represents a missed opportunity, with RM39.59 billion worth of projects recorded over three years. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said only 468 contractors were registered under the F01 and F02 facility management specialisations, despite 1,541 facility management and maintenance projects being recorded by the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) between 2023 and 2025. Ahmad said facility management had previously received less attention because contractors and the industry traditionally focused on construction and regarded maintenance as a secondary activity.

items.title: Malaysia's economy beats expectations with 5.7pc growth, says Finance minister II
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Malaysia’s impressive economic growth in the first half of the year, which exceeded Bank Negara Malaysia’s 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) projection of four to five per cent, demonstrates the resilience of the country’s economy. Finance Minister II, Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, said GDP grew at a rate of 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of this year and six per cent in the second quarter, resulting in an overall economic growth of 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026. “In fact, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) also raised Malaysia’s GDP forecast from 4.3 per cent in January 2026 to 4.7 per cent in April 2026.

items.title: Poor management, financial weakness behind 75pc of delayed projects, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 18 — An estimated 75 per cent of delayed and sick construction projects nationwide are due to weak management, poor operational oversight and financial shortfalls, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan today. He said technical issues at project sites made up the remaining 25 per cent which showed the need for contractors to strengthen their financial position, internal management and ability to deliver projects. He said CIDB records showed that Bumiputera contractors made up 47,064, or 72 per cent, of the 65,446 Grade G1 contractors registered nationwide.

items.title: Court directs Tun M to file Batu Puteh RCI report as fresh evidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today directed Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad to file an application to introduce the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the Batu Puteh sovereignty issue as fresh evidence in his appeal. The three-member panel comprising Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun gave Dr Mahathir's lawyer, Zainur Zakaria, two weeks to file the application. Earlier, Zainur told the court that the RCI report showed Dr Mahathir was the subject of the inquiry into the handling of the Batu Puteh issue.

items.title: Malaysia wary of BYD disrupting auto market as in Thailand – Ong Kian Ming
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The automotive industry is in a state of flux, as investments by Chinese automakers in Malaysia and Southeast Asia are disrupting their respective markets, causing governments to scramble to respond in order to protect their local players. Taylor's University adjunct professor Dr Ong Kian Ming said while the impact of most Chinese carmakers' plans in Malaysia could be anticipated by the government, BYD Auto's plans are shifting the debate among ministers. "BYD came in with certain proposals that I think were maybe anticipated by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) but not anticipated by other members of the government.

items.title: Cabinet to table comprehensive plan to strengthen entry point controls tomorrow
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A comprehensive plan to improve controls at the country's entry points will be tabled at the Cabinet meeting tomorrow, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the plan would be jointly presented with Transport Minister Anthony Loke, as it included matters under the jurisdiction of the Transport Ministry. He said the plan was prepared within two weeks following a Cabinet directive to strengthen controls at the country's entry points through greater coordination among relevant agencies.

items.title: Consider random breathalyser tests for pilots, cabin crew
items.summary: LETTERS: THE recent incidents of pilots who tested positive for drug abuse should prompt airlines to raise their bar in regional screening to maintain public trust and aviation safety standards. The recent two incidents in Asia have highlighted that human factors remain a critical vulnerability in safe aviation operations. The first, on July 28 at Jakarta's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport, involved a co-pilot after a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta on a 737-800, who tested positive for methamphetamine.

items.title: 1,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes found in bread consignment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 39-year-old Malaysian man was arrested in Singapore after allegedly attempting to smuggle 1,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes into the country in a Malaysia-registered lorry. The Singapore Immigration and Checkpoints Authority said the contraband was uncovered after its officers flagged the vehicle for enhanced checks at the Tuas checkpoint on Aug 11. "A 39-year-old male Malaysian was arrested in connection with the case," it said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Home minister: Malaysia’s entry points to get security boost after drug scandal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — A comprehensive plan to enhance security at the country’s entry points will be presented to the Cabinet tomorrow, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the plan would be jointly presented with Transport Minister Anthony Loke at the meeting. The plan was prepared within two weeks following a Cabinet directive to strengthen controls at the country’s entry points through the coordination of various relevant agencies.

items.title: More companies advertise jobs, but offerings fall 11.4pct in Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of online job offerings advertised in Malaysia fell 11.4 per cent to 555,509 in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026 from 626,816 in the preceding quarter, the Statistics Department said. Professionals accounted for the largest share of online job offerings at 51.5 per cent, or 285,907 positions, down 9.5 per cent from 315,768 in the previous quarter. Managers followed with 87,950 job offerings, while technicians and associate professionals recorded 86,512.

items.title: Bus Cap surges 80pct in three days, blows past analysts' fair values
items.summary: It opened 3.9 per cent, or 1.5 sen higher at 39.5 sen from Monday's close of 38 sen. Over the three sessions, the counter has gained 80.77 per cent, or 21 sen, from last Thursday's close of 26 sen. It rose 25 per cent to 32.5 sen last Friday before climbing another 16.9 per cent to 38 sen on Monday. Against its IPO price of 23 sen, the stock has gained 104.3 per cent and is 49.2 per cent higher than its first-day closing price of 31.5 sen.

items.title: Amir Hamzah: Tough economic reforms necessary despite unpopularity
items.summary: The Finance Minister II said reforms implemented by the government included electricity subsidy rationalisation from 2023, the expansion of the Sales and Services Tax (SST) and the phased implementation of the e-Invoicing system. Amir Hamzah said the phased implementation of electricity subsidy rationalisation had not affected the majority of Malaysians, with 85 per cent of domestic users remaining protected. Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's economy remained on a strong footing, with gross domestic product (GDP) growing 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 and six per cent in the second quarter, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent.

items.title: Bond yields jump, oil extends gains as US-Iran ceasefire expires
items.summary: The yield on the US 30-year Treasury bond rose as much as 1.1 basis points to an intraday high of 5.321 per cent, its highest in almost 20 years. Its 10-year counterpart traded up 0.4 basis point at 4.724 per cent. S&P 500 e-mini futures slumped 0.2 per cent as MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slid 0.3 per cent, reversing early gains as stocks in Taiwan and China weighed on the benchmark.

items.title: Temerloh crash: Fuel tanker driver claims trial over mother, son's deaths
items.summary: TEMERLOH: A fuel tanker driver claimed trial at the magistrate's court here today to two counts of dangerous driving that resulted in the deaths of a mother and her son at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang last week. The accused, who was driving the tanker, was charged with dangerous driving that resulted in the death of 39-year-old Nur Fatimah Syuhada Abdullah. On the second charge, Nor Azlan was charged with dangerous driving that resulted in the death of Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal Saifulnizam, 12, at the same location and time.

items.title: [UPDATED] Fire Skills Hub to strengthen first response before firefighters arrive
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Building operators are being trained to become the Fire and Rescue Department's "eyes, ears, hands and feet" during emergencies under a nationwide programme to strengthen fire safety at premises. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the Fire Skills Hub was designed to equip personnel at designated premises with practical skills to respond before firefighters arrive. He said the initiative, developed in collaboration with HRD Corp, would support the appointment and development of fire safety managers and fire safety officers at premises gazetted under fire certification requirements.

items.title: RTS Link aims to fast track immigration clearance in a matter of seconds
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link service is expected to take only several seconds to complete a passenger’s immigration procedure once it isfully operational by early next year. Mass Rapid Transit Corporation’s (MRT Corp) RTS Link project director Zulkifli Mohamed said passengers do not need to queue long for these procedures as there are 100 e-gate lanes at the Bukit Chagar Integrated Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex. The four-kilometre RTS Link will connect Bukit Chagar station in Johor Bahru to Woodlands North station in Singapore.

items.title: [UPDATED] Fire and Rescue Dept monitoring 62 locations at risk of major fires
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Fire and Rescue Department is closely monitoring 62 locations nationwide at risk of large-scale fires covering more than 25ha amid a sharp rise in open fires this year. Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the locations were among 183 hotspots identified nationwide as being prone to open fires based on records from the past five years. Nor Hisham said the 62 locations were receiving particular attention because fires there could spread rapidly and require substantial mobilisation of firefighting resources.

items.title: Finance Ministry says e-invoices, though unpopular, are necessary to rein in shadow economy
items.summary: Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan pointed to e-invoicing among others, a policy that he said is crucial to shrink the size of the country’s massive shadow economy but was met some grumbling from mostly small enterprises. “The effort to restructure the economy is not an easy task. The size of Malaysia’s shadow economy, also referred to as the underground or informal economy, is estimated to be roughly 21 per cent to over 30 per cent of gross domestic product, depending on the estimation methodology and reporting period.

items.title: [UPDATED] Fire and Rescue Dept mulls home EV charging guidelines after Cheras blaze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Fire and Rescue Department may introduce safety guidelines for electric vehicle (EV) charging at private homes following Sunday's fire at a house in Cheras. Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said there were currently no specific guidelines governing EV charging installations at private homes. However, Nor Hisham said investigators had yet to conclude that the EV itself caused the Aug 16 fire in Cheras.

items.title: Philippine student killed in school shooting
items.summary: MANILA: A student was shot dead at a Catholic junior high school in the Philippines on Tuesday before the alleged shooter took his own life, a mayor in the country's south said. "A (seventh-grader) managed to enter carrying a high-powered firearm and a .45-calibre pistol," Zamboanga City mayor Khymer Olaso told a local radio station. It seems he missed, then moved to another room... he shot another student there, the one who fell," Olaso said, referencing a screen-grabbed video being circulated by local media.

items.title: 2027 Budget to ease cost of living, boost economic resilience
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 2027 Budget will prioritise easing cost-of-living pressures, strengthening social protection and improving education, healthcare and basic services while boosting Malaysia's economic competitiveness and resilience. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the fifth Madani Budget, which is set to be tabled on Oct 9, would focus on three broad priorities. Amir Hamzah said the government would also prioritise food security, business productivity and fiscal sustainability.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM AUGUST 18, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, shrugging off Wall Street's weak overnight performance as buying interest lifted most sectors. In the crypto market, Bitcoin rebounded to RM261,502. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: RM23,000 cash prizes up for grabs in Malaysia Day competitions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Total cash prizes of RM23,000 are among the main attractions of a series of competitions held in conjunction with the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations, in an effort to further foster patriotism among Malaysians. Communications Ministry Strategic and Corporate Communications Division assistant secretary Muhammad Khairul Nazmi Jamsari said the initiative comprises two main categories, namely the Lensa Malaysia Photojournalism Competition and the AiMAGINASI Malaysia Competition. Under the theme ‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’, this year’s National Day celebrations will be held in Putrajaya, while Malaysia Day celebrations are scheduled to take place in Sarawak.

items.title: Crude extends gains, stocks stagger as Mideast hopes dim
items.summary: HONG KONG: Oil prices extended gains and stocks stuttered Tuesday as a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained distant, a day after the deadline for a truce between the foes expired. "He'll make the right deal when the right deal is ready," he added. Earlier, Trump said Iranian officials "want to make a deal, but they're not going to make the kind of a deal that I feel is necessary".

items.title: Abolition of AUKU will foster critical thinking in universities, says G25 civil society group
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The proposed abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) would foster a culture of independent and critical thinking within the country’s higher learning institutions, says civil society organisation G25 Malaysia. The group of prominent retired civil servants welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s assurance that any replacement law would not restrict the rights and freedoms of university students, noting that youth empowerment had to begin in higher education. It said the legislation also needed to include proper disclosure of appointments and qualifications, safeguards against political patronage and conflicts of interest, and clear standards governing the responsibilities and independence of boards.

items.title: Get ready, students: 2026 SPM schedule to be announced today
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 18 —The 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination schedule is expected to be announced this evening after receiving the approval of Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek, said Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad. He said the proposed improvement to the examination schedule would be presented by the deputy director of the Examination Syndicate to Fadhlina today for consideration and approval. He said the preparation of the new schedule took into account the views of various parties, including concerns regarding the status of several examination papers which were previously often scheduled at the end of the examination period.

items.title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to embrace ‘Aku Berjanji’, strengthen spirit of patriotism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has urged all Malaysians to listen to and embrace the National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 theme song titled “Aku Berjanji”. In a post on his official Facebook page yesterday, Fahmi said the song, composed and performed by renowned singer Faizal Tahir, could further strengthen the spirit of love for the country. Earlier, Fahmi received a visit from Faizal in Putrajaya, during which the singer also shared updates on his upcoming concert, scheduled for Oct 3 at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil.

items.title: Dollar feeble as rate hike bets dwindle, Iran war worries grow
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The US dollar held near multi-month lows against most major currencies on Tuesday as traders walked back expectations of near-term monetary tightening, although the imminent threat of an escalation in the Middle East war left sentiment fragile. The euro fetched US$1.1581 in early Asian hours, not far from the two-month high of US$1.1614 it touched on Monday. Data showed last week that US retail sales fell in July for the first time in nine months, following unexpected job losses last month and mild inflation readings.

items.title: Firefighters battle hill forest blaze near Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah mosque
items.summary: “Fire tenders from the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arriving at the location found about seven acres (2.8 hectares) of hilly forest on fire. He said 10 officers and personnel were involved, using fire beaters and water pumps to fight the fire. “Firefighters are extinguishing remaining hot spots using water sourced from the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) fire hydrant, supported by a water tanker, alongside creating fire breaks to prevent the fire from spreading,” he said.

items.title: Education DG: SPM schedule to be announced today [WATCH]
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination schedule is expected to be announced this evening after receiving the approval of Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek, said Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad. He said the proposed improvement to the examination schedule would be presented by the deputy director of the Examination Syndicate to Fadhlina today for consideration and approval. He said the preparation of the new schedule took into account the views of various parties, including concerns regarding the status of several examination papers which were previously often scheduled at the end of the examination period.

items.title: Gold extends gains on easing rate-hike fears, markets await Fed minutes
items.summary: Spot gold was up 0.2 per cent at US$4,424.28 per ounce by 0130 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.2 per cent higher to US$4,480.90. The US dollar lingered around multi-month lows against most major currencies. Platinum inched 0.2 per cent higher to US$1,772.75, while palladium was down 0.3 per cent at US$1,330.05.

items.title: Japan's Nikkei slides as Middle East stalemate fuels oil, inflation concerns
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average fell on Tuesday, putting it on course to snap a five-day winning streak, as a stalemate in the Middle East conflict drove oil prices higher and renewed concerns about bond market risks and inflation. The Nikkei dropped 1.1 per cent to 68,460.56 by late morning, after a 5.5 per cent gain over the previous five trading sessions. The broader Topix eased 0.2 per cent to 4,177.50.

items.title: US Navy destroyer left without power for four days in South China Sea
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The USS Benfold, an Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer, was left without power for four days in the South China Sea last month following an engineering failure, Anadolu Ajansi reported. "On July 24, 2026, while conducting routine operations in the Indo-Pacific, Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Benfold (DDG 65) reported an engineering casualty involving its generators, causing a loss of power," Cmdr Matthew Comer, a spokesperson for the US 7th Fleet, told USNI News in a statement. Comer said the George Washington Carrier Strike Group, with which the Benfold had been sailing, supported the destroyer during the incident.

items.title: TH welcomes move to amend Act, committed to strengthening governance
items.summary: The amendments, TH said, would help strengthen governance and ensure the responsibilities entrusted to TH continue to be upheld. "TH will continue to support every improvement effort to strengthen the trust of depositors and ensure that this trust continues to be preserved for future generations," it said in a post on TH's official Facebook yesterday. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a post on Facebook, said the government would implement amendments to the TH Act 1995 to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be preserved.

items.title: SkyeChip's AI expansion to yield meaningful earnings from 2029
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SkyeChip Bhd's expansion into artificial intelligence (AI) silicon and Arm-based compute platforms is expected to contribute limited revenue in the near term, UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd said. "In the meantime, SkyeChip's established silicon intellectual property (IP) and custom application-specific integrated circuit (Asic) businesses should remain the key earnings drivers," it said in a note. The firm said SkyeChip's recent engagement with Cerebras Systems for custom interface IP demonstrated the company's ability to participate in advanced AI computing platforms.

items.title: 99 Speed Mart poised for stronger second half
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd is expected to deliver stronger earnings in the second half of financial year 2026 (FY26), supported by seasonal spending and continued store expansion. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said resilient demand for essential goods should also support the convenience store operator's earnings despite cautious consumer sentiment. "Despite softer consumer spending, we believe 99 Speed Mart's essentials-heavy and value-oriented positioning should support resilient demand, with additional benefits from consumer downtrading and higher in-home consumption," he said in a research note.

items.title: ‘Change must come from the top’: Ex-deputy IGP says it is up to leaders to combat corruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Efforts to combat corruption and strengthen integrity comprehensively require strong political will beginning from the highest level of leadership, says former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay. He said top leadership must lead by example and demonstrate firm resolve, as any form of organisational transformation would only succeed if those at the top sent a clear signal of having zero tolerance for misconduct. “Change must come from the top.

items.title: Tabung Haji backs law amendments to boost governance and preserve depositor trust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 —The Tabung Haji (TH) Board welcomes the government’s move to amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995, in line with the recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), to strengthen governance in ensuring that the responsibility entrusted to it continues to be preserved. “TH will continue to support every improvement effort to strengthen the trust of depositors and ensure that this trust continues to be preserved for future generations,” it said in a post on TH’s official Facebook yesterday. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a post on Facebook, said the government would implement amendments to the TH Act 1995 (Act 535) to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be preserved.

items.title: Unhealthy air alert: Johan Setia in Klang hits API 157
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Air quality in Johan Setia, Klang dipped to an unhealthy level this morning, with the area recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 157 at 8am, according to national air quality data. Berita Harian reported that across the country, 64 monitoring stations reported moderate air quality, while three locations in Kedah (Alor Setar, Langkawi) and Perlis registered good readings. Under Malaysia’s API scale, readings of: 0–50 indicate good air quality 51–100 moderate 101–200 unhealthy 201–300 very unhealthy Above 300 hazardous The figures are updated hourly from 68 monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Driver in fuel tanker crash that killed two to be charged in Temerloh today
items.summary: TEMERLOH. Aug 18 — The driver of a fuel tanker involved in a horrific crash that killed a mother and her 12‑year‑old son on Jalan Temerloh–Triang last Friday is expected to be charged in the Temerloh Magistrate’s Court this morning. The tanker driver sustained minor injuries.

items.title: Police raid in Kampung Bukit Rangin unveils ketum leaves stockpile, 187.5kg seized
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 18 — Police arrested a married couple suspected of processing and selling ketum water at a house in Kampung Bukit Rangin here on Sunday, with ketum leaves and related items seized valued at RM15,745. Kuantan police chief ACP Ashari Abu Samah said the couple, aged 52 and 62, were arrested during a raid at about 4 pm following information from the public. "Police also seized 1,150 transparent plastic packets containing 187.5 kilogrammes (kg) of ketum leaves, as well as various items believed to have been used to produce ketum water,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Police nab two in RM1.66m cigarette contraband bust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Police arrested two men believed to be involved in a syndicate storing and distributing contraband cigarettes, with items worth RM1.66 million seized during Ops Taring Alpha 1 in the Klang Valley yesterday. “In total, we seized 2,115 cartons of various brands of suspected unpaid duty cigarettes, along with two vehicles and five mobile phones believed to be connected to the illegal activities,” he said in a statement today. Mohd Zaki said the value of the seized cigarettes and goods was RM1,499,852, while the total value of all seizures, including related assets, was RM1,661,352.

items.title: Foreign minister in Manila for Philippines-Malaysia joint commission meeting
items.summary: MANILA, Aug 18 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan arrived here tonight to lead the Malaysian delegation at the ninth Philippines-Malaysia Joint Commission Meeting (JCM), today. Upon arrival, he was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino, while Wisma Putra Deputy Secretary-General (Bilateral Affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin and other officials welcomed him at the hotel. During the meeting, Mohamad will co-chair the session with Philippines Foreign Secretary Ma.

items.title: Umno vice-president: Party, BN committed to see through partnership in government until end of term
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) remain committed and serious about fulfilling their roles and responsibilities in the Federal Government until the end of the current parliamentary term, says Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. Mohamed Khaled, who is also Defence Minister, said that although BN had contested against Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) in the previous series of state elections, BN did not use the results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan as a reason to withdraw its commitment. “Differences in administration at the state level do not prevent good cooperation at the Federal level.

items.title: Explainer: What makes a by-election necessary in Malaysia, and when it is not?
items.summary: By-elections are held when a seat falls vacant for reasons other than the dissolution of Parliament. Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution requires a by-election to be held within sixty days from the time the EC gets notified about a vacant seat. A seat becomes vacant if the incumbent resigns, gets expelled, passes away or gets disqualified from holding office.

items.title: Selangor waits for Putrajaya to register Myanmar refugees before deciding next steps
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 17 — The Selangor government is awaiting the Home Ministry’s registration of Myanmar refugees and stateless individuals under the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) before deciding on further measures to manage the community in the state. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state government was currently compiling data on the community at the district level to be submitted to the Home Ministry, enabling follow-up action to be taken with relevant agencies and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). He said the state government had no authority to issue licences or permits to the community to carry out certain activities, as the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the Federal Government, particularly the Home Ministry.

items.title: Viral sword threat in Langgar lands Kedah-born man in Perlis police custody for three days
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 17 — Police detained a 46-year-old man over a viral social media post allegedly containing a threat to injure an individual with a sword. Perlis acting police chief SAC Zaihairul Idrus said the Kedah-born suspect was detained in Langgar yesterday and remanded for three days from today. “Police recovered the sword shown in the viral post from the suspect’s vehicle during the arrest.

items.title: No licence, no insurance, so no Mercedes: Langkawi JPJ seizes Bangladeshi farmer’s luxury ride
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 17 — The Kedah Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized a Mercedes-Benz vehicle used by a Bangladeshi man during Ops Luxury around Jalan Padang Matsirat, Langkawi, yesterday. In a statement today, Kedah JPJ director Stien Van Lutam said the 38-year-old man, who works as a vegetable farmer, had been using the vehicle since May 27, 2025. “Checks revealed that he did not have a valid driving licence, while the motor vehicle licence (LKM) had expired and the vehicle had no insurance coverage, which lapsed on July 26,” he said, adding that the vehicle was subsequently seized.

items.title: RM3.4m bill stands for former MARA Corp CEO after appeal fails over 25 hires
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — The Court of Appeal has upheld the High Court’s decision in ordering Majlis Amanah Rakyat Corporation Sdn Bhd (MARA Corporation) former group chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Badlisyah Abdul Ghani to pay RM3.4 million to the company for breaching his contractual, fiduciary and statutory duties. A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Ahmad Fairuz Zainol Abidin had dismissed Badlisyah’s appeal and affirmed the High Court’s decision. The court also ordered Badlisyah to pay RM50,000 in costs.

items.title: High Court lets Aliff Syukri defer apology to ex-minister Abdul Kadir in RM30m investment suit pending appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The High Court today allowed businessman and cosmetics entrepreneur and social media personality Datuk Seri Aliff Syukri Kamaruzaman’s bid to defer his apology to veteran politician Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Sheikh Fadzir in a RM30 million investment debt suit. Aliff Syukri’s lawyer, Mahmud Abdul Jumaat, confirmed the matter after proceedings on the stay of execution before Judge Roslan Mat Nor. On April 29, Judge Roslan ordered Aliff Syukri to pay RM250,000 to former Minister of Culture, Arts and Tourism Abdul Kadir, after allowing the suit filed by Abdul Kadir against him.

items.title: 1MDB ex-CEO Shahrol says no deal to escape US$5.64b civil suit, no explanation given too
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today he has no idea why the company dropped him from its US$5.64 billion civil suit. He revealed this during cross-examination by lawyer G.K. Ganesan, who represents former 1MDB investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jin, the seventh defendant in the suit. Shahrol Azral: Correct.

items.title: Fahmi: Pakatan leaders to meet on PKR congress and DAP conference outcomes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) leaders will hold a meeting soon to discuss several matters identified following the PKR National Congress and DAP Party Conference, including efforts to accelerate reforms and address violations of the law and major scandals. PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the messages conveyed by delegates at the PKR congress and DAP members at the conference were clear that reform efforts must be expedited and firm action taken on issues involving breaches of the law and major scandals. “The message conveyed by the delegates at the Keadilan Congress and members at the DAP Conference was very clear that efforts to advance reforms must be accelerated and firm action must be taken, including on issues involving violations of the law and major scandals.

items.title: High Court to deliver ruling next February on Daim family bid to lift account freeze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The High Court today fixed Feb 22, 2027 to deliver its decision on a judicial review application filed by the family of the late Tun Daim Zainuddin, seeking to lift the freeze on their bank accounts by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). Judge Norliza Othman set the date after hearing submissions from lawyer Abraham Au, representing Daim’s family, while Senior Federal Counsel (SFC) Nurhafizza Azizan appeared for the MACC and five other respondents. Eighteen companies are also named as applicants, namely Aad Equity Sdn Bhd; Yayasan Haji Zainuddin; Ilham Baru Sdn Bhd; Anchor Point Sdn Bhd; Kangkung Catering Sdn Bhd; Adrihaniz Sdn Bhd; Syarikat Maluri Sdn Bhd; Amiraz Sdn Bhd; Ridana Sdn Bhd; Daan Sdn Bhd; Maya Seni Holdings Sdn Bhd; Magical Zone Sdn Bhd; Permatang Maju (M) Sdn Bhd; Brainstorms Sdn Bhd; Arida Farms Sdn Bhd; Gajah3 Resource Centre Sdn Bhd; Ilham Tower Sdn Bhd, and Selidik Jaya Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Judge rules Caprice defamed Ebit, orders apology and RM200,000 compensation
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — The Shah Alam Sessions Court today ordered social media personality Ariz Ramli, better known as Caprice, to pay RM200,000 in damages to preacher Ebit Irawan Ibrahim Lew in a defamation case. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the ruling was delivered by Judge Zuhrina Nor, who found that Caprice had defamed the preacher in 2023 through seven statements made with Indonesian influencer Mondy Tattoo. The court granted a seven day ad interim stay on the damages payment to allow Caprice time to file a formal stay application, should he choose to appeal to the High Court.

items.title: Zahid chairs road safety panel, maps congestion fixes before Johor Bahru RTS January debut
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — Plans are being drawn up to ease traffic congestion in Johor Bahru city centre and prevent new bottlenecks from emerging ahead of the launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plans involved coordination among agencies and integration of public transport systems, as travel patterns were expected to change, particularly around the city centre and areas directly connected to the system. The system will connect Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru with Woodlands North in Singapore.

items.title: Alam Damai house goes up in flames, Bomba suspect EV charging in foyer the cause
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A two-storey terrace house in Alam Damai, Cheras, here, was destroyed in a fire early yesterday morning believed to have been caused by an electric vehicle (EV) that was being charged in the foyer of the house. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations division assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar in a statement today said his department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 5.03 am before a team of personnel from the Cheras, Sungai Besi and Bandar Tun Razak Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were rushed to the location. Ahmad Mukhlis said upon arriving at the location of the incident, his department found that the two-storey terrace house was 100 per cent burnt down.
